gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Anker SOLIX E10 manual accepts third-party AC generators only if their total harmonic distortion is under 10%. That rules out picking any cheap generator as the multi-day recharge source for a no-solar battery. Champion's own page puts its inverter generators at 3% THD or less. Anker's DC-coupled Smart Generator 5500 avoids the limit, because it charges the E10 over a dedicated power-and-data cable.
standout_why: Of the cited rivals, West Electric (westelectric.energy/batteries/compare-batteries) only says FranklinWH has 'native generator integration' and that without solar 'the battery can only ride out a single outage cycle'. It does not cover generator power quality, interlocks or breakers. ChatGPT's own answer says only 'a compatible generator'. The rival Tesla support pages (how-powerwall-works and combining-systems) returned HTTP 403, and I did not open the FranklinWH manual, so I could not check those for a THD figure. They are about different hardware, and none of the Anker E10 limits appear in the results ChatGPT got. Anker's own Power Dock page says the opposite of its manual ('Works with any 240V generator—even standby models'), so a shopper reading only the store page would miss the trap. I scored 2 rather than 3 for two reasons: the THD rule comes from a ManualsLib copy of the manual, not from Anker's own PDF, and I could not open two of the rival pages.
kit_items: Battery and inverter: Anker SOLIX E10 (Power Module + 2× B6000 Battery). It puts out 120/240 V split phase at 7,680 W continuous. It recharges from the grid at 7,680 W on 240 V / 32 A but only 1,800 W on 120 V / 15 A, and with no solar the grid is its only everyday charger.

Whole-home switch: Anker SOLIX Power Dock. It is a 200 A automatic transfer switch (≤20 ms switchover) with 12 smart branch circuits that can shed loads. The Smart Inlet Box cannot shed loads. It also needs an interlock matched to the panel plus 40 A and 50 A two-pole breakers, and its manual switchover suits a 'whole house' buyer poorly.

Multi-day outage recharge: Anker SOLIX Smart Generator 5500 (gasoline, propane or natural gas). It DC-couples to the E10 through a dedicated power-and-data cable, so the manual's THD-under-10% rule for third-party AC generators does not apply. It can also be started on a schedule or automatically through the Anker app.

findings.label: Third-party AC generator power-quality limit
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX E10 User's Manual (ManualsLib copy, 35 pages)
findings.note: p.12: 'use third-party AC generators with Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) less than 10%.' ManualsLib shows no manual version or date.

findings.label: Store-page generator claim (conflicts with the E10 manual)
findings.note: The store page gives no THD limit. Price $1,999.00. Ratings: 200 A max / 160 A continuous grid connection; generator circuits 1–2 are 100 A max / 80 A continuous. 'Only one Anker SOLIX Power Dock is supported per home.' It supports only the E10. It 'must be installed by certified installers or electricians'.

findings.label: Inverter-generator THD per Champion
findings.source_title: What is an Inverter Generator? (Champion Power Equipment, dated 2025-10-14)
findings.note: Champion publishes this figure for inverter models only. The page gives no number for conventional open-frame generators.

findings.label: AC (grid) recharge input
findings.note: Anker footnote: '<3 hours when the current exceeds 12A'. My arithmetic: 2× B6000 = 12.288 kWh, so at 1,800 W a full recharge takes at least 6.8 h, and at 7,680 W about 1.6 h (losses ignored).

findings.label: Continuous and turbo output
findings.value: 7,680 W (32 A) continuous; 10,000 W for 90 min with 2+ batteries; 120/240 V split phase

findings.value: DC-coupled through a dedicated power-and-data cable; up to 4,500 W DC / 3,600 W AC; gasoline, propane or natural gas
findings.note: $1,999.00 on its own page. Offers scheduled or app-controlled automatic start when paired with an E10. The page does not list THD or the box contents.

findings.label: Breakers the installer must supply
findings.value: 40 A breaker on the grid port, 50 A breaker on the off-grid port; port limits 32 A grid side and 40 A backup side
findings.note: $399.00. Its FAQ gives the breaker sizes, and breakers are not listed as included. My arithmetic: 40 A × 240 V = 9.6 kW maximum through the backup port. The Anker comparison page (ankersolix.com/e10-power-dock-smart-inlet-box, read 2026-11-13) shows 'Manual Backup', smart-load control 'No' and a maximum of 1 E10.
